title: Prefetch & Priming Profiles — brain dump
body:
Quick brain dump: prefetch / priming profiles for session-aware inference

Goal: reduce tail latency and token cost for common conversational flows by proactively warming model KV cache + applying lightweight priming tokens based on predicted next intents. Target hosted API first (cheap wins), then Dedicated.

Why this might matter:
- Many apps have recurring conversational patterns (login, booking flow, FAQ triage) where first-user prompt triggers heavy compute (long context rebuild). Warming KV cache for likely next-turn shapes can shave 40–200ms on 1-3 token responses and larger on streaming output.
- Prefetch combined with compact priming (50–200 tokens) can reduce repeated token generation variability and make hallucination rates more consistent across shards.

Core ideas / components:
1) Priming profiles (server-side): small, model-agnostic prompt fragments that standardize context setup for a session type. Examples: onboarding-short, billing-clarify, search-refine. Stored as named, versioned snippets.
2) Prefetch triggers: heuristics and lightweight classifiers (edge or control plane) that predict likely next-turn profile and request prefetch to serving pool. Signals: route, user metadata, previous N messages embedding similarity, event hooks (page load, button hover).
3) Warm PV/KV cache: when prefetch triggered, issue a low-priority inference call with priming tokens to populate KV for the model instance(s). Should be marked with low quota priority, no billing to customer for speculative warm (internal cost)? Need policy.
4) Cache scoping & eviction: tag warm state by (model variant, profile-version, routing key, session-id TTL). Eviction TTL tunable (default 60s). Reuse across sessions for same tenant if tenant-level isolation allows.
5) Safety & correctness: priming must not leak private data. Profiles are templates only. Prefetch requests must not include PII from customers unless explicit opt-in for private deployments.

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer I want the API to accept a "priming_profile" header so I can ask Redwood to apply a named priming snippet for a session.
- As an app developer I want Redwood to automatically prefetch a priming_profile on page load for authenticated users so first-response latency is improved.
- As an SRE I want metrics on prefetch hit rate, extra cost per prefetch, and latency delta on warmed vs cold requests.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics for MVP:
- Implementation exposes 3 priming profiles (onboarding-short, faq-refine, small-system).
- Pre-warm path reduces median first-byte latency by >= 50ms on target benchmark workload (web chat typical).
- Prefetch cost overhead <= 10% of token consumption for warmed sessions across a 24h window (configurable throttle).
- No PII present in priming snippets; audit check integrated into console.

Implementation sketch / API ideas:
- POST /v1/prefetch with body { model, profile_name, scope: [session|tenant|global], priority: low|normal } — returns request id and estimated warm TTL. (internal-only for now)
- Header X-Redwood-Priming: "profile=onboarding-short;version=2" — server will apply server-side priming on incoming generation.
- Console: Priming profiles UI under Console -> Optimize -> Priming profiles; quick preview + diff against profile versions.

Routing & runtime considerations:
- Warmed KV is per-model-instance. To get benefit, prefetch must be routed to same placement pool that will serve the real request. Use smart routing hint: when client pins region/tier, prefetch route accordingly. For Dedicated this is simpler; hosted will need probabilistic routing with affinity windows.
- Fallback: if warm not available, serve cold as usual. Visible metric in trace for decision.

Safety & billing policy notes:
- For hosted API: keep speculative prefetch as billable by default but with "prefetch_budget" controls on account and team level. Consider free speculative budget for new users to improve onboarding.
- For Dedicated / Private: allow customers to opt-in to allow prefetch server-side (since concerns about cost).

Experiment ideas (A/B):
- Control: no prefetch. Variant A: prefetch on request arrival. Variant B: prefetch on UI event (hover). Variant C: only apply priming header but not pre-warm. Metrics: time-to-first-token, completion-accuracy (eval suite), cost delta, user engagement (success rate).

Open questions / decisions: (TODO)
- How to measure correctness impact (quality drift from priming)? Need small eval harness per profile with holdout prompts.
- Policy on free vs billable prefetch. Finance ops opinion required.
- Edge classifier placement: run tiny model on edge to predict profile vs route decision to control plane. Latency trade-offs.
- Multi-tenant warm sharing: allowed? default no for isolation; opt-in for sharing might get big wins. Need legal/security sign-off.

Next steps (short):
- Spike: prototype prefetch endpoint + simple "onboarding-short" priming snippet for gpt-ish.open-llama-variant. Measure latency impact on low-traffic test app. (owner: me)
- Draft console prototype wires (Marco) and permission model.
- Create JIRA tickets: implement prefetch endpoint, priming profile store, dashboard metrics.
- Sync with finance/legal for billing/PII guardrails.

Notes to self:
- Keep priming snippets <200 tokens initially. Avoid long system messages that could push token context out.
- Consider combining with KV prefix caching system we already have — might be able to reuse existing cache tags. Check with serving-runtime team.
- This is a ripe area for Redwood Optimize recommendations: suggest profiles based on historical session traces.

References / short links:
- CONFLUENCE: priming-patterns-2024 (internal)
- JIRA: INFR-4821 (prefetch routing affinity)
- Slack: #optimize-discuss thread 11/01/24

Random brainlets: what about "cold-synthesis" where we synthesize a single synthetic token sequence representing the canonical next-turn tokens and warm that — cheaper than full priming? Worth experimenting.

End of dump. Will refine into proto PRD once spike data arrives.
